Equitable Hiring and Retention Review Rubric
A systems check on who gets hired, developed, retained, and advanced.
Purpose

Review the tools that shape workforce decisions - position descriptions, screening, interviews, onboarding, development - for avoidable barriers, including barriers for candidates and staff with disabilities. This tool reviews systems; individual personnel decisions remain with HR and management.
When to use this tool
Writing or revising a position description or posting.
Designing interviews, scoring rubrics, or screening criteria.
Reviewing why hiring, retention, or advancement patterns look uneven.
Position descriptions and postings
☐  Requirements are actual requirements - not inherited wish lists that screen out capable people
☐  Degree and years-of-experience demands are justified or replaced with demonstrable skills
☐  Plain language throughout; jargon and insider acronyms removed
☐  Accommodation statement is prominent, welcoming, and true
☐  Posting travels beyond the usual channels - community organizations, disability employment networks
Screening and interviews
☐  Criteria and scoring anchors are written before reviewing any candidate
☐  Panels are diverse, and every panelist uses the same questions and rubric
☐  Interview logistics are accessible by default: format choices, materials in advance, accessible locations and platforms
☐  Questions test the job, not cultural polish - “culture fit” is replaced by defined, job-relevant values
☐  Notes record evidence against criteria, not impressions
Onboarding, development, retention
☐  Accommodations process is fast, respectful, and does not depend on self-advocacy stamina
☐  Development opportunities and stretch assignments are posted, not quietly handed out
☐  Mentorship is open to all - see the program's voluntary mentorship strand
☐  Exit and stay patterns are reviewed by group at the aggregate level, and findings produce system changes

Boundaries

Do not record client, case, medical, legal, or other identifying information in this document. Tribal Nation consultation follows established government-to-government channels. This tool supports staff judgment; it does not replace program, legal, HR, or leadership responsibility. For tailored guidance, request a consultation with the Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant.
